introduced.event_name: NCC 1983 — planned ERA² and Logix Athena premiere
introduced.timeline_note: Planned premiere on the opening day of NCC, 16–19 May 1983; not a confirmed shipment date.

data.product_status: Accepted 1983 planning baseline; implementation, memory fit and release qualification pending.
data.description: ROM-backed successor to AIONix: protected preemptive multitasking, documented ERA ABI compatibility, recoverable HDD storage, user access management and an event-driven TUI designed for later graphical windowing.
data.delivery: At least 256 KiB directly executable shared OS ROM, alongside at least 256 KiB DRAM. EEPROM BIOS remains boot/diagnostic firmware. Optional services, larger utilities and patches load from disk; do not copy the entire OS ROM into RAM.

rom_execution.mapping: Shared read-only executable mappings; private writable data per process. Cacheable ROM with independently qualified timing.
rom_execution.updates: Versioned dispatch tables and page-sized RAM patch overlays; ROM version/checksum checks and recovery boot bypassing disk patches. Patched pages consume DRAM.
rom_execution.physical_implementation: 256 KiB minimum system ROM bank; chip organization, package count, board mounting and timing remain qualification decisions.

compatibility.scope: Documented ERA AIONix user binaries, instruction semantics and C ABI; not Z80 binary compatibility.
compatibility.mechanism: Executable ABI version selects legacy adapters; stable library dispatch and capability discovery.
compatibility.limits: Undocumented kernel dependencies, privileged drivers and direct hardware access require separate qualification; portable Z80 C applications require recompilation.

multitasking.kernel: Compact monolithic kernel; timer-preempted user processes, bounded non-preemptible kernel critical sections.
requirements: Checked user pointers and protected kernel/device mappings
Process-exit cleanup of files, memory, locks and child state
Per-process memory, file and request limits
Short interrupt handlers with deferred work
Kernel-controlled DMA with checked pinned buffers
multitasking.limits: Process isolation does not isolate kernel/driver faults or independently constrain DMA. Fully preemptible kernel and application threads are not initial requirements.

posix_direction.reference: POSIX.1-2024 / Issue 8, used as an out-of-world future-informed design reference, not a 1983 certification claim.
initial_target: Consistent open/read/write/close/lseek/stat and descriptor duplication, inheritance and errors
Reliable existing copy-on-write fork, exec, wait, exit status and environment
Defined signal delivery, masks, dispositions and interrupted-call semantics
Canonical/raw terminal modes, terminal attributes and foreground process groups
Hierarchical paths, working directories, hard links and symbolic links
Pipes with EOF/broken-pipe semantics and readiness multiplexing
Shell quoting, redirection, pipelines, variables and exit statuses
Wall clock, monotonic elapsed time and explicit timestamp formats
later: Efficient spawn without replacing fork semantics
Broader file control and memory mapping
Broader utilities, locales, threads and timers
posix_direction.conformance: Publish per-interface implemented/partial/absent matrix and unsupported-operation errors; names alone do not establish conformance.

filesystem.design: Versioned inode-based filesystem; directory entries separate from metadata.
filesystem.qualification_note: Testing range, not capacity ceiling or a change to bundled HDD sizes.
requirements: Ownership, permissions, link counts and timestamps
Mount support and logical-sector driver interface with CHS translation when required
Clean/dirty volume state and consistency checker
Ordered metadata writes and explicit synchronization
Backup/restore utilities and defined durable-save ordering
filesystem.later: Small metadata journal after write-order and power-loss testing; journal does not by itself guarantee application-data durability.

initial_target: Numeric users and groups
Owner/group/other read/write/execute and directory search permissions
Creation masks
Real/effective credentials
Login sessions and home directories
Protected password database with salted costed hashing selected against CPU budget
Administrative control of devices, mounts and configuration
Kernel enforcement on all relevant operations
Protected administrative audit records
user_access.privilege: Qualify credential and exec transitions before enabling set-user-ID programs. Server authenticates identity rather than trusting client-supplied UID.
user_access.later: Extended ACLs and more elaborate policies.

ui_layers.name: Application layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Business logic and semantic commands such as Open, Save, Select and Cancel, independent of rendering.

ui_layers.name: Abstraction layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Events, menus, forms, lists, focus, layout, text measurement and drawing contexts.

ui_layers.name: Translation and compatibility layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Existing TUI adapters, terminal rendering, device backends and legacy ABI behavior; later graphical renderers.

ui_layers.name: OS native API
ui_layers.responsibility: Processes, files, IPC, timers, input devices and controlled display access.

ui_contract.implementation: Logical layers primarily in shared libraries plus a small UI service; not four mandatory processes or IPC crossings. Extend the existing portable C API.
initial_target: Unified bounded event queue for keys, timers, focus, redraw and future pointer events
Semantic commands separated from physical keys
Opaque window/view handles initially representing text regions
Clipping, invalidation and repaint requests
Layout constraints and explicit text measurement
Separate cell and pixel coordinates
Bounded clipboard and selection ownership
Capability/version discovery for graphics, fonts, color and pointer input
ui_contract.memory: Compact text state, dirty regions and redraw callbacks; no mandatory full-screen RAM backing bitmap.
ui_contract.next_generation: Windowed GUI; legacy character applications run in terminal windows. Adapters do not automatically redesign old UIs.

memory_management.initial: Shared ROM code, sparse page tables, small kernel stacks, reliable copy-on-write and graceful allocation failure.
memory_management.later: Controlled disk-backed paging/swap only after restart, locking and I/O qualification; keep fault handlers and essential paging state resident.
memory_management.policy: Swap handles occasional pressure, not a routinely oversized working set; ROM does not replace writable RAM.

qualification: Measured ROM/RAM footprint and Abacus/compiler/server workloads
TUI capability fallback and legacy terminal behavior

priority_assessment.feasibility: Strong existing foundation; fit and patch behavior must be measured.
Feasible with ERA protection and restart rules; extensive verification.
20–100 MB addressing is straightforward; crash recovery is the main risk.
Phase interfaces; full contemporary conformance excluded.
Depends on proven faults and I/O; not initial release gate.
Not required in the minimum 1983 configuration.

release_scope.initial: ROM execution, documented legacy ABI, protected preemptive processes, recoverable HDD storage, users/permissions, POSIX-oriented subset and event-driven TUI groundwork.
release_scope.later: Paging/swap, metadata journal, broader networking/threads/locales and full windowed GUI.
release_scope.schedule: Retain planned NCC announcement; no new shipment date or completed implementation claimed.

resource_planning.basis: Engineering allocation target, not a measured fit or maximum. Server retains its existing 1 MiB configuration.

data.name: AIONix 2 (ERA² edition)

minimum_resources.status: Recorded requirements only; unspecified limits remain unknown.
